title: Gene Duplication Tree
goal: A practitioner can visually assess the Gene Duplication Tree scenario using its published diagram convention.

rubric.must: A rooted branching tree visibly shows the stated sister taxa and their clade relationships.
Horizontal branch lengths visibly vary to encode the supplied evolutionary distances.
The named taxa are legible at the tree tips.
The named clade is visibly highlighted distinctly from the rest of the tree.
A visible scale or distance label identifies the evolutionary-distance interpretation.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the phylo/rectangular exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The target shows a rooted rectangular tree with Human and Mouse tips paired within GeneA and GeneB, visibly unequal horizontal branch lengths, an orange GeneA clade, readable tip labels, and a 0.05 substitutions/site scale. The dashed label extensions are identified as alignment guides that add no branch length, so connections remain traceable.

items.evidence: A root splits into GeneA and GeneB pairs; Human GeneA and Mouse GeneA are sisters, as are Human GeneB and Mouse GeneB.
Horizontal branches visibly differ in length, with the two clade stems and individual tip branches represented separately.
All four tip labels—Human GeneA, Mouse GeneA, Human GeneB, and Mouse GeneB—are legible.
GeneA is distinctly highlighted in orange, including its tree branches and clade bracket; GeneB remains dark.
A scale bar is labeled “0.05 substitutions/site,” and the caption identifies horizontal distance as substitutions/site.
